look_here_first: Tall nearly glabrous dioecious amaranth with long-petioled leaves and long terminal spikes; pistillate plants have sharp bracts longer than the tepals.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local + 3 wild iNaturalist observations; Kew accepts species native from southern California to Texas and Mexico.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for visual learning; only current native-range evidence should feed native metrics.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Amaranthaceae/Amaranthus: alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny unisexual flowers. Habit, plant sex, hairiness, nodal spines, cluster position, bract/tepal form, and fruit dehiscence are high-value characters.
best_field_traits: pistillate bracts 4–6 mm and longer than tepals
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Tall, smooth, dioecious Palmer contrasts with hairy monoecious redroot pigweed. No paired nodal spines.
